section_summary: This section contains Japanese fiscal 1938–39 budget tables, supplementary loan laws, and provisions for financing military expenditure connected with the Japan–China conflict. It also records subsidies, guarantees, and continuing appropriations for shipping, aviation, agriculture, public works, overseas administration, and debt service. The section begins and ends within longer budget enclosures.

subfiles.title: Extraordinary expenditure budget table, concluding pages
subfiles.about: The concluding table itemizes extraordinary spending across Japanese government departments.
subfiles.summary: The table lists departmental appropriations for justice, education, agriculture, commerce, communications, overseas affairs, and health and social affairs. It ends with total extraordinary expenditure of ¥1,227,260,554 and combined ordinary and extraordinary expenditure of ¥2,867,796,855.

subfiles.title: Law No. 21: Supplementary loans for fiscal year 1938–39
subfiles.about: Authorizes additional loans or borrowings for general-account expenditure.
subfiles.summary: Law No. 21 permits up to ¥73,100,000 in supplementary borrowing for 1938–39.

subfiles.title: Law No. 22: Transfers from special accounts to temporary military expenditure
subfiles.about: Provides for transfers from several special accounts to finance the Japan–China conflict.
subfiles.summary: Law No. 22 directs transfers from communications, railways, and overseas-administration special accounts to temporary military expenditure, with later reimbursement from the general account.

subfiles.title: Law No. 23: Transfer of special-account tax revenue to military expenditure
subfiles.about: Allocates overseas-administration tax and monopoly receipts to temporary military expenditure.
subfiles.summary: Law No. 23 transfers 80 percent of specified tax and tobacco-monopoly receipts, plus special conflict taxes, from Kwantung, Chosen, Taiwan, and Karafuto accounts.

subfiles.title: Law No. 24: Increased borrowing for the Japan–China conflict
subfiles.about: Raises the borrowing ceiling for temporary military expenditure.
subfiles.summary: Law No. 24 increases the authorized ceiling under Law No. 84 of 1937 from ¥2,022,700,000 to ¥6,476,200,000.

subfiles.title: Supplementary general-account budget for fiscal year 1938–39
subfiles.about: Sets supplementary general-account revenue and expenditure at ¥386,492,330.
subfiles.summary: The budget lists tax and loan revenues and directs ¥317,165,276 to the temporary military expenditure special account.

subfiles.title: Supplementary special-account budget for fiscal year 1938–39
subfiles.about: Details supplementary revenues and expenditures in departmental and overseas special accounts.
subfiles.summary: Tables cover loans, national debt amortization, military arsenals, communications, railways, and the administrations of Kwantung, Chosen, Taiwan, and Karafuto. They show transfers to temporary military expenditure and substantial loan proceeds assigned to that account.

subfiles.title: Supplementary urgency military budget
subfiles.summary: Sets revenue at ¥4,886,591,321 and expenditure at ¥4,850,000,000 for war, naval, and reserve purposes.

subfiles.title: Supplementary general budget and continuing-expenditure table for fiscal year 1938–39
subfiles.about: Sets a ¥171,005,858 supplementary budget and revises multiyear appropriations.
subfiles.summary: The budget authorizes equal supplementary revenue and expenditure of ¥171,005,858, including ¥153,819,023 in loans. The surviving pages also revise continuing allocations for forestry, drainage, reclamation, industrial laboratories, navigation marks, and aviation.

subfiles.title: Extra budget for fiscal year 1938–39: leases, agriculture, aviation, and Manchukuo guarantee
subfiles.about: Authorizes multiyear financial commitments across several departments.
subfiles.summary: The budget covers foreign-mission leases, shipbuilding loan support, land-reclamation subsidies, and pensions. It sets terms for subsidized Tokyo–Peking, Fukuoka–Nanking, and international air services, including government rights to use aircraft in emergencies. It also authorizes a guarantee on Manchukuo development and colonization debentures.

subfiles.title: Extra budget for fiscal year 1938–39: China recovery, disaster relief, shipping, and oil
subfiles.about: Provides guarantees and subsidies for businesses, shipping, disaster work, and oil exploration.
subfiles.summary: The budget supports loans to restore Japanese businesses and shipping affected by the China conflict and funds civil engineering after disasters. It provides export indemnification, guarantees debentures for North Sakhalin oil exploration, and authorizes subsidies for large passenger ships. It also extends a Chosen property-loan indemnification period.

subfiles.title: Extra budget for fiscal year 1938–39: public works and departmental commitments
subfiles.about: Lists multiyear subsidies, guarantees, contracts, and detailed departmental expenditures.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure No. 7 schedules subsidies for named river and harbor works, disaster rehabilitation, Hokkaido development, and other public works. It authorizes debenture guarantees for northeastern development enterprises, credit subsidies, army and navy contracts, and agricultural commitments. Its later tables detail ordinary and extraordinary spending by department, ending with total expenditure of ¥171,005,858.

subfiles.title: Supplementary general budget estimate for fiscal year 1938–39
subfiles.about: Sets an additional ¥89,226,372 in revenue and expenditure.
subfiles.summary: The budget relies chiefly on loans and provides for development companies in North and Central China, disaster relief, foreign trade, shipbuilding subsidies, government information work, and protection of wounded soldiers.

subfiles.title: Supplementary special-accounts budget for fiscal year 1938–39
subfiles.about: Details additional revenues, expenditures, and continuing appropriations for special accounts.
subfiles.summary: The tables cover the mint, printing office, debt fund, public loans, universities, communications, and the administrations of Chosen, Taiwan, Karafuto, and the South Seas. Continuing appropriations include weather reporting, reconstruction of Akita postal facilities, and telegraph and telephone installations in Chosen.

subfiles.title: Budget Table B: continuing expenditure
subfiles.about: Revises continuing appropriations for river and harbor works.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure No. 5 lists prior, additional, and future allocations for riparian work and several harbors. The table continues beyond page 148.
